audit.whatIsWrong: Chart said Skill at level 1 where whys[0] says Yone pokes freely and Sylas has no answer, gave Yone levels 2 and 3 where the whys describe a manageable bait-and-chain pattern, and only Skill at level 6 where the Hijack is described as swinging the lane. Packet chart reads Yone, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill on a 51.6% (853 games) near-even matchup.
audit.why: Yone's 4-second Q dash beats Sylas before E exists. From 2 onwards it is close, gated by Soul Unbound's 22-second rank-1 cooldown. Level 6 is the one clean Sylas swing since a stolen Fate Sealed costs nothing while his own is 120 seconds.
audit.corrected: Rows realigned to Yone, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill in both layers.

audit.why: Four spikes: Yone's level 1-2 window, level 6 Hijack, Riftmaker, and Yone's two-item spike. The level 6 entry's description was wrong (point 4) but the timing is right.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten with Fate Sealed's real behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed is called 'a massive line knockup' in two places and the player is told to 'line it up behind him to cancel his rewind path'. Riot's text says Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls all enemies hit toward him — a pull, not a knockup, and the kit carries no knockup flag on R (the knockup is on his two-stack Q). Spirit Cleave (W) is absent from the entire page despite being a 14-second cone that shields him. Soul Unbound's cooldown is never stated and is called a 'fifteen-second invitation' when it is 22 seconds at rank 1.
audit.why: A player expecting a knockup will plan a follow-up that never gets its CC, and the rewind-cancel line is a mechanic I could not verify anywhere in the data. Spirit Cleave's shield is what makes a counted-lethal Sylas burst come up short.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed restated as a blink-behind that drags everyone hit toward you, with its 120-second cooldown; the rewind-cancel claim removed rather than replaced; Spirit Cleave's 14-second shield written into whys[2] and the mid text; Soul Unbound stated at 22 seconds.
sources: _kits/yone.json Q (knockup at 2 stacks), W (14s, shield), E (22/19/16/13/10), R (120/100/80, dash only)

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup-defining cooldown is correctly identified as Soul Unbound but its length was wrong everywhere it appeared.
audit.why: 22 seconds at rank 1 dropping to 10 at rank 5 changes the advice completely across the lane — early it is a window you can plan around, late it is barely a window at all.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into early, mid and dosFull[2].d.

audit.why: wants.you[2] said to force the all-in 'while he has no knockup to re-engage with' — his two-stack Mortal Steel is a knockup and is always available, so the premise was false.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to key off his R's 120-second cooldown instead, which is the real reason the level 6 window exists.

edits.before: Full kit is live but his E escape is still the governor — bait Soul Unbound with a step-up, then chain him before the rewind timer expires.
edits.after: Spirit Cleave shields him every 14 seconds and Soul Unbound is his exit — bait the E with a step-up, then chain him before the rewind returns him.

edits.before: Hijack Fate Sealed immediately — it is a massive line knockup that strips his best engagement tool and gives you the all-in opener he just lost.
edits.after: Hijack Fate Sealed immediately — it blinks behind the last champion in a line and drags everyone hit back to you, and his own copy is 120 seconds.

edits.before: Hijack steals Fate Sealed — a massive line knockup — turning Yone's kill-setup into your engage tool and swinging every all-in.
edits.after: Hijack steals Fate Sealed — a blink behind the line that pulls everyone hit toward you — turning his kill setup into your engage.

edits.before: You have no real answer to his level 1 Q dash poke — he can dash in, auto-Q, and back off faster than your Q slow or hook can punish. Stand near the minion wave to make his Q dash angles tighter and last-hit with Q from distance. At level 2 your E comes online but he can still burn Soul Unbound to trade and rewind before you hook — only commit the E2 chain if his E is visibly on cooldown or he has overextended past the minion line.
edits.after: You have no real answer to his level 1 Q dash poke — he dashes in, auto-Qs, and backs off faster than your Q slow can punish, and his Q is on 4 seconds. Stand near the minion wave to tighten his dash angles and last-hit with Q from distance. At level 2 your E comes online, but Soul Unbound is a 22-second escape at rank 1 and he can trade then rewind before you hook — commit the E2 chain only when his E is down or he has overextended past the minion line.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the steadiest stretch: your W heal lets you absorb his Q trades and your passive chain autos chunk him back in extended exchanges, but Soul Unbound remains his get-out card — if you hook him mid-E he still rewinds, so bait the Soul Unbound first by stepping up aggressively, then hook the empty body after he commits. At 6 the matchup swings — Fate Sealed is an exceptional Hijack: line it up behind him to cancel his rewind path, and every all-in becomes yours to dictate.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the steadiest stretch: your W heal absorbs his Q trades and passive chain autos chunk him back, but Soul Unbound — 22 seconds at rank 1, down to 10 at max — remains his get-out card, and Spirit Cleave shields him every 14 seconds on top of it. Count both before you commit: bait the E by stepping up hard, then hook once he has spent it. At 6 the matchup swings, because Fate Sealed is an exceptional Hijack — a blink behind the line that drags everyone hit back to you — and every all-in becomes yours to dictate.

edits.before: Steal Fate Sealed at level 6 and force an all-in while he has no knockup to re-engage with
edits.after: Steal Fate Sealed at 6 and force the all-in while his own copy sits on 120 seconds

edits.before: Yone burns Soul Unbound on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Yone burns Soul Unbound on nothing — take the twenty-two-second invitation.

notes: Spirit Cleave (W) did not appear anywhere on this page — a 14-second cone that shields him is exactly the thing that makes a counted-lethal all-in fail, and it is now stated. Fate Sealed was described twice as a knockup; per Riot's text it is a blink-behind that pulls, and Yone's only knockup is his two-stack Mortal Steel. I deleted the 'line it up behind him to cancel his rewind path' instruction rather than rewriting it — I could not verify any such interaction and did not want to replace one invention with another. Kraken Slayer and Navori references in the late text were left alone as item claims I cannot check against the kits.
